title: Chip Morning Brief
tldr: Chips are being stacked, not just shrunk: Samsung is aiming for hybrid bonding in 2027.
AI agents are entering chip design, but humans still sign off.
Packaging and memory, not just transistors, now limit AI chips, so money is flowing there.

cards.head: Samsung bets on gluing chips together with copper

happened.t: Samsung targets early 2027 to develop 3D Cube-H hybrid bonding, with a 6 µm interconnect pitch, for AI processors and HBM.
A paper calls hybrid and fusion wafer bonding foundational for both 'More than Moore' integration and 'More Moore' transistor scaling.
Fine-pitch probing (EOTPR) can isolate die-to-die interconnect defects in chiplet devices.

cards.basics: Old way: a chip hangs on tiny solder balls (flip-chip). Hybrid bonding presses copper pads directly onto each other, so the connections can be much closer together. Closer connections mean more wires between stacked chips, which means more bandwidth for less energy.
cards.ai: If connections get this dense, designers will probably have to plan die-to-die links and test access from the first day of a design, not at the end.

cards.head: AI agents are joining the chip-design team, on a leash

happened.t: Agentic AI automates engineering workflows and widens design exploration while engineers keep oversight and verification.
Orchestration, security, data privacy and reliability must improve before agents get more autonomy.
Synopsys, Hiveware, Silvaco and Axiomise name integration, expertise retention, data protection and cost as challenges.
Siemens will acquire Lauterbach to combine chip verification with software debugging in its EDA portfolio.

cards.basics: EDA is the software engineers use to design chips: write the logic (RTL), simulate it, check it (verification), then lay it out. 'Shift left' means catching bugs earlier in that chain, because a bug found after manufacturing costs far more.
cards.ai: Routine checking and exploration will likely be automated first, so a beginner's edge may shift toward writing clear specs and judging whether the AI's results are right. Learn RTL and verification basics anyway.

cards.head: The real AI bottleneck is moving data, not computing

happened.t: Edge AI inference drives memory designs that cut data movement, such as processing-in-memory and near-memory computing.
Larger models and longer context windows strain memory capacity, bandwidth, latency, power and cost.
Samsung is reportedly developing custom HBM4E for Meta, with customer-specific functions in a 2 nm base die.
With memory scarce, better test, repair and reliability raise the number of usable dies.

cards.basics: HBM is a tower of memory chips sitting right beside the processor. The chip at the bottom of the tower (base die) handles the connection; putting a customer's own logic there means memory is becoming part of the chip design itself.
cards.ai: Architects may increasingly be judged on how little data their design moves, not only on raw speed.

cards.head: Packaging is now where AI chips get built, and the money followed

happened.t: Intel signed its first external 18A-P foundry customer and named Microsoft as first customer for EMIB packaging.
ASE is investing NT$100 billion in two Kaohsiung plants for advanced AI chip packaging, aiming at 5,000 jobs.
SPIL partnered with Nvidia to triple Taiwan's advanced packaging capacity by mid-2029.
Nvidia is also investing over US$1 billion in Kinsus to expand substrate manufacturing.

cards.basics: Packaging means assembling finished chips into a working module. ASE and SPIL do this for others (they are OSATs).
cards.ai: With this much Taiwan capacity planned, packaging skills may become a regional career advantage for chip engineers.

cards.head: Chips stay scarce into 2027, maybe 2028

happened.t: SMIC sees tight capacity through 2027, with equipment lead times of 16-24 months.
SEMI expects silicon wafer shipments to grow 11.8% in 2026, driven by AI, memory and fab expansion.

cards.basics: A new fab needs equipment ordered up to two years ahead, so shortages cannot be fixed quickly.
cards.ai: Scarcity may keep chip prices and the value of efficient designs high for a while.

cards.head: Washington tightens the rules on AI chips for China

happened.t: The US requires licences for overseas data centres serving Chinese firms.
TSMC halted advanced orders below 16 nm from Chinese chipmakers without US licences.
Nvidia stopped shipping licensed Hopper AI chips to China.

cards.ai: Expect more compliance work for Taiwan's chip firms.

cards.head: Nvidia's CEO leaves, yet the supply chain shrugs

happened.t: Nvidia reported record Q3 revenue of US$115.8 billion under an interim CEO.
Experts expect little disruption to Taiwan's supply chain from the Nvidia leadership change.

cards.ai: Demand for AI chips looks stronger than any one person.

cards.head: TSMC buys into the AI labs, and the numbers don't match

happened.t: TSMC set up a US$500 million investment company to take stakes in chip-ecosystem firms.
Another report says TSMC plans up to US$1 billion in OpenAI and Anthropic.
A later report says TSMC bought a 0.03% Anthropic stake for US$500 million.

cards.flag: The reports give different amounts and are not reconciled; they may describe different things (a fund versus specific stakes).
cards.ai: Treat the exact figures with caution until the original filings are checked.

take: The bottleneck has moved from transistors to connections: bonding, packaging and memory.
AI helps design chips but is supervised, so fundamentals (RTL, verification) still matter.
Scarcity through 2027 supports investment in Taiwan's packaging.
